brandGuidelines.title: Logo Clear Space
brandGuidelines.rule: Always maintain clear space around the logo equal to the height of the 'B' in 'BLUE'. No other elements should intrude within this protected zone.
brandGuidelines.doExample: Logo with adequate breathing room on all sides — nothing within the clearspace zone.
brandGuidelines.dontExample: Logo crowded by text, borders, or other design elements within the clearspace.

brandGuidelines.title: Logo on Photography
brandGuidelines.rule: When placing the logo on photography, ensure sufficient contrast. Use the White or Gold & White version on dark imagery, Black or Gold & Gray on light imagery.
brandGuidelines.doExample: White or Gold & White logo on dark food photography with clear visibility and contrast.
brandGuidelines.dontExample: Color logo on busy mid-tone photography where it becomes difficult to read.

brandGuidelines.title: Color Application
brandGuidelines.rule: Black is the dominant surface color. Gold is reserved for logo variants and premium accent elements. Crimson is used sparingly for high-impact emphasis. Never use Crimson as a background or large-area fill.
brandGuidelines.doExample: Black background with Gold logo and limited Crimson accent on a key callout.
brandGuidelines.dontExample: Crimson or Gold used as dominant background colors across large areas.

brandGuidelines.title: Typography Pairing
brandGuidelines.rule: Always pair Lapture Display Bold for headings with Boston for body copy. Lapture Display headings are always uppercase — never sentence case or title case. Never use Lapture Display for extended paragraph text. Boston Bold can be used for menu item names and strong in-body labels.
brandGuidelines.doExample: LAPTURE DISPLAY UPPERCASE HEADLINE with Boston Regular paragraph text below.
brandGuidelines.dontExample: Lapture Display in sentence case, or used for body copy or any text requiring extended reading.

brandGuidelines.title: Logo Modifications
brandGuidelines.rule: Never modify the logo by stretching, rotating, adding effects, or applying unapproved colors. Only the four approved color variants (Gold & Gray, Black, White, Gold & White) may be used.
brandGuidelines.doExample: Logo used in one of the four approved color variants at correct proportions.
brandGuidelines.dontExample: Logo stretched, outlined, shadowed, tilted, or recolored in any unapproved way.
